[Date]

To: Appeals Department  
[Medicaid managed-care plan name and appeals address or fax number]

Re: Appeal of denial of total knee replacement  
Member: Quinn Novak  
Member ID: W666121456  
Reference number: POC-638643858B-53234  
Requested service: Total knee replacement  
CPT code: 27447  
Date of denial notice: August 23, 2026

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I request reversal of the denial of my prior authorization for total knee replacement, CPT 27447. The denial states that the submitted records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The clinical records do document an extensive and unsuccessful trial of conservative treatment, as summarized below.

I have had 12 months of progressively worsening knee pain that has not been relieved by rest. I completed 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy from March 15, 2026, through July 5, 2026, including 16 visits focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion. The completed course and lack of adequate improvement are documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

I also used NSAIDs for six months, with inadequate relief. On June 4, 2026, I received a corticosteroid injection, which produced only two weeks of partial relief. These treatments were not successful in controlling my symptoms or restoring function.

The objective findings support the need for surgery. Weight-bearing radiographs dated July 1, 2026, show bone-on-bone apposition in the medial and patellofemoral compartments, lateral joint-space narrowing, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 osteoarthritis. Examination documents varus alignment, crepitus, effusion, and restricted motion from 5 to 100 degrees.

The condition substantially interferes with daily activities and sleep. I cannot climb stairs without assistance and wake three to four times each night because of pain. These findings demonstrate persistent symptoms and significant functional impairment despite medication, supervised therapy, and injection treatment.

The records also document that there is no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker. The requested procedure is being recommended by Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery, based on the documented symptoms, failed conservative treatment, examination findings, imaging, and functional limitations.

Please reconsider and approve the requested total knee replacement. At minimum, please provide the specific medical-necessity criteria and clinical-review criteria applied to this request, identify the governing policy relied upon, and explain precisely which required criterion the submitted records allegedly fail to satisfy. The denial notice does not identify the managed-care organization, policy title, policy number, or the specific clinical-review criteria used. The plan has not been quoted in this appeal because the notice does not provide those criteria.

Please also consider the attached or previously submitted records:

1. Physical therapy discharge note documenting 16 completed visits from March 15, 2026, through July 5, 2026.
2. Medication history documenting six months of NSAID treatment with inadequate relief.
3. Procedure record documenting the June 4, 2026, corticosteroid injection and only two weeks of partial relief.
4. Weight-bearing knee radiographs dated July 1, 2026.
5. Orthopedic examination and treatment plan from Reyes, MD.
6. Clinical documentation of impaired stair climbing, sleep disruption, pain duration, and failed conservative treatment.

Please treat this as a formal appeal and confirm receipt. The denial notice states that the appeal must be received by February 19, 2027. Please send the appeal decision and any further appeal rights in writing.

Sincerely,

Quinn Novak
